findings.reason: a node that follows the reuse instruction builds the resolver on an enumerator that cannot produce §2's answer, so the section's done-when is unreachable as written; the author must name what is actually reused (reading the `session` field off live pointers and ledger rows) or drop the reuse clause.
findings.text: §2 ends "The resolver is one function beside obligations.py's session filter, which it reuses", and the only session filter §2 cites is `_live_review_runs` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:467-476`), which iterates `runs.list_live(project=…)` and keeps only pointers whose `session` matches **and** whose current revision has a review in flight (`if run_id and _current_review_in_flight(pointer)`); §2's answer instead needs "the session of its most recent dispatched run, live or in the ledger" — and its done-when runs on a fixture built from a *committed* ledger — so a resolver that reuses that function sees no ledger row at all and drops every live run without a review in flight, reporting nearly every plan unowned and failing §2's own first negative control

findings.reason: the symbol is named and resolves in the same file, so a reader greps it; correcting the line number refreshes the citation without changing what §2 asks a node to build.
findings.text: §2 cites `reckon/crew/obligations.py:429` as `_live_review_runs` and as the evidence that a session filter already exists, but line 429 sits inside `_refused_delivered_review` and the named function is at `reckon/crew/obligations.py:467`, so a reader following the line lands on unrelated code

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — `reckon/crew/obligations.py:429` does not contain `_live_review_runs` (that function is at line 467; line 429 lies inside `_refused_delivered_review`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the measure is a fixture assertion with two declared negative controls (all-unowned must fail; dispatch-order-ignoring must fail), and the gate log is required to name the deciding row and which of `plan`, `plan_link` or the node id matched, so the expectation is not sourced from the derivation under test.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 names only "the gate log" and directs no evidence to a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols are named by mechanism ("the resolver"), and §2 carries no ticket number, version tag or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the mechanism §2 states for building the resolver (reusing `obligations.py`'s session filter) reuses a function that enumerates only live runs with a review in flight, so it cannot produce the answer §2's own done-when requires.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable: derive a plan's coordinator session from the ledger beside its `plan-owner`.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `s2` declares no `depends-on` of its own, and every section that consumes its answer declares it (`s3` and `s5` name `a-coordinator-sees-the-board#s2`; `s4` reaches it through `#s3`).
